land.text: the northern half of the divided Chenla, 'located in Isan (northeast Thailand)'

predecessors.note: The Tang histories date the split 'shortly after 706', after 6 February 707; Cliopatria's row begins in 718.

land.text: the northern lands: 'Land Chenla maintained its integrity under Jayavarman II, who proclaimed the Khmer Empire in 802'

successors.note: The Chenla page does not describe a formal unification; Cliopatria's Khmer Empire row begins in 800, its Land Chenla row runs to 805.

capitals.name: Mueang Fa Daet Song Yang (Kalasin), outer capital of Wendan
capitals.note: The page lists three disputed identifications: Pelliot, Sambhupura; Coedes, Wen Tan; Hoshino, Wendan's 'outer capital at Mueang Fa Daet Song Yang (Kalasin) and inner capital at Kantharawichai (Maha Sarakham)'. Hoshino's is drawn because it lies inside the Isan outline (Sambhupura, on the Mekong at Sambor, lies south of it). The dot is at Kalasin town (researcher's coordinates), not the site.

correction.text: The same outline, drawn from 707 (years only): Isan, southern Laos and northern Cambodia.

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 707-799, not 718-799. The Tang histories date the split 'shortly after 706' (after 6 February 707; infobox 'Land-Water separation: c. 707') and both halves sent tribute separately in 717, so the shape holds from the split; Cliopatria's chenla_710 shape (710-717) is the union of this and Water Chenla. The 183,796 km2 outline is the same as Chenla's pre-627 northern shape; 'Land Chenla is located in Isan (northeast Thailand)'. The page gives no km2 figure.

correction.text: The same outline, ended in 802 (years only).

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 800-802. The page has Jayavarman II proclaiming the Khmer Empire in 802 (infobox 'Jayavarman II proclaimed as chakravatin: 802'; the Khmer Empire page: 'conventionally dated to 802'), so the Land Chenla shape ends there, not 805. The outline is unchanged apart from a 1,000 km2 trim.

region.text: the northern half of Chenla, in Isan

ledger.note: c. 707: Chenla splits and Land Chenla (Wendan) forms in the north. 'shortly after 706, the country was split into Land Chenla and Water Chenla' (New Book of Tang), after 6 February 707 by the Tang histories; 'Land Chenla is located in Isan (northeast Thailand)'.

802: Land Chenla passes into the Khmer Empire. The page says Land Chenla 'maintained its integrity under Jayavarman II, who proclaimed the Khmer Empire in 802'; the Khmer Empire page: the empire 'grew out of the former civilisation of Chenla'. The page is silent on how Land Chenla joined.

wars.name: Mai Thuc Loan's rebellion (722-723)
wars.outcome: The page records only that Land Chenla's embassy of 722-723 'aided' the rebellion; the result and any change of border are not on it.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; no territorial result.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a frontier; the Isan outline and its Mekong and Champa edges are approximate.

sources.title: Chenla
sources.note: Identity, the c. 707 split, Land Chenla in Isan, the three capital proposals, 717 tribute, 722-723 embassy, 798 last mission, 802. No km2 figure.

sources.title: Jayavarman II
sources.note: Jayavarman II and the 'Java' of the inscriptions possibly Wen Dan, 'the Land Chenla polity'; no formal unification of the halves described; 802 consecration at Mount Mahendraparvata.

sources.title: Khmer Empire
sources.note: 'The beginning of the Khmer Empire is conventionally dated to 802'; the empire 'grew out of the former civilisation of Chenla'; silent on a Land/Water distinction.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Land Chenla' row is the northern half of the Chenla of Wikidata Q1057118; written as its own state because the Chinese sources treat Land and Water Chenla as separate realms from c. 707 (see the chenla dossier's notes). Moved from Cliopatria: start 707 (not 718); end 802 (not 805), the Khmer Empire's conventional founding year. Not settled: the capital (three disputed identifications on the page, only Hoshino's drawn); what happened to Land Chenla between the last Chinese mission of 798 and 802; the Seshat page (kh_chenla) was not opened. The Jayavarman II page notes the Woodward/Ferlus proposal that the inscriptions' 'Java' is Wen Dan, i.e. Land Chenla; not used. Counterparts: chenla (this batch); khmer-empire (se-01 part a/other; should carry the gain of Land Chenla in 802).
